feedback.goal: Wire OpenAI, Anthropic, Z.ai, and Kimi into the e2e driver through the in-box dsh-llm-pi-ai adapter and document the exact configuration.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A provider registry maps openai/anthropic/zai/moonshotai to their catalog routes, credential envs, and default fast-tier models.
Non-deepseek providers emit an llm-pi-ai composition row declaring the route with its apiKeyEnv.
A missing provider key fails the run before any model call, and the key is passed into the container environment only.
The batch manifest digest binds --provider so each provider/model pair requires its own decision.
benchmarks/tau-style-workflow/PROVIDERS.md documents wiring, digests, key flow, and failure mode.
Live pass@k batches actually run on each provider.

outcome.summary: Multi-provider wiring is implemented, unit-tested, and documented. Live provider batches are a pending verification step that depends on human-supplied API keys and per-provider approval decisions; the wiring itself is complete.

what_worked: dsh-llm-pi-ai is mounted dormant by dsh-base; declaring a providers profile in a composition row registers the route live, and catalog routes ship endpoint/protocol/model catalogs for all four targets.
The pinned demo image carries the same adapter at the same harness version.

calls.name: docker
calls.purpose: Probe the pinned demo image for the dsh-llm-pi-ai adapter.

evidence.summary: tests/e2e-providers.test.ts: 6/6 passed (registry, pi-ai row emission, deepseek exclusion, unknown-provider rejection).
Documents provider table, llm-pi-ai row wiring, digest flow, run command, and credential failure mode.

uncertainty.statement: Live batches per provider are unrun: OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ZAI_API_KEY / MOONSHOT_API_KEY and per-provider approval decisions are human-supplied.
uncertainty.resolution: Run per-provider batches with --provider/--model once the keys and decisions exist.
